newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dransfield to raise HK$27 mln to cut debt.
newsitem.headline: Dransfield to raise HK$27 mln to cut debt.

text.p: Consumer electronic goods and appliances marketer Dransfield Holdings Ltd plans to raise HK$27.4 million through an issue of 60 million new shares, it said in a statement published on Tuesday.
Proceeds raised will be used to reduce short term borrowings and to strengthen the capital base of the company, it said.

Dransfield said four companies controlled by chairman Kenneth Fung and deputy chairman Horace Cheong had agreed to privately place a total 20 million existing shares, or 5.18 percent of existing share capital, at HK$0.465 per share.
They would then subscribe for a total 40 million new shares at the same price, it said.
Dransfield also said it had agreed to place another 20 million new shares to independent investors at the same price.
The total 60 million new shares represent 13.45 percent of the comapny's expanded share capital, it said.
On completion of the placement and subscription, aggregate shareholding of the four companies controlled by Fung and Cheong will be reduced to 52.96 percent from 56.01 percent.
Shares of Dransfield were untraded at HK$0.475 on Tuesday after a one-day suspension on Monday.
